recorded_by: hostless replay against 732 timestamped migrations, PGlite 0.5.5 / PostgreSQL 18.3
notes: `failed` is the ONLY gate. CI fails when the FAILED count rises above it.
Raising this number is a deliberate act: do it in the same commit as the
migration that caused the rise, and say here why the rise is acceptable.
Lowering it is free and should be done whenever a run reports fewer.
The one known failure at this baseline:
could not find a function named "assign_admin_role"
The file REVOKEs and GRANTs on a function it does not create and that no
earlier migration creates either. It existed in the live database before
the history was captured, so the history has never been self-contained
here. Pre-existing, not a regression, and it changes no schema object.
not counted: it carries no timestamp prefix, so it has no position in the
history. It is a staged production change awaiting review, not a migration.
